title: Password Entropy Estimator
description: Estimate theoretical password entropy from an assumed character set. This is an approximation, not a crack-time guarantee.
code:
import math

length = 16
charset_size = 26 + 26 + 10 + 10  # example: letters, digits, symbols
entropy_bits = length * math.log2(charset_size)
print('Estimated entropy bits:', round(entropy_bits, 1))

title: Create a Salted SHA-256 Demo Hash

title: Offline Dictionary Audit of a Toy Hash
description: Compare a toy SHA-256 salted hash against a tiny local wordlist. This is an intentionally limited offline demonstration.
code:
import hashlib

known_password = 'summer-demo'
salt = bytes.fromhex('00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff')
target = hashlib.sha256(salt + known_password.encode()).hexdigest()

candidates = ['winter-demo', 'summer-demo', 'spring-demo']
for candidate in candidates:
    test = hashlib.sha256(salt + candidate.encode()).hexdigest()
    if test == target:
        print('Toy lab match:', candidate)
        break
else:
    print('No match in this tiny test list')

title: Demonstrate Why Unique Salts Matter
description: Show that identical passwords produce different salted hashes.
code:
import os, hashlib
password = b'demo-password'
for _ in range(2):
    salt = os.urandom(16)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(salt + password).hexdigest()
    print('salt:', salt.hex(), 'hash:', digest)

title: PBKDF2 Password Storage Demo
description: Use PBKDF2 with a random salt for a learning example; prefer a modern password-hashing library and reviewed parameters in production.
code:
import os, hashlib, base64
password = b'Example-Only-Password'
salt = os.urandom(16)
rounds = 600_000
digest = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', password, salt, rounds)
print('rounds:', rounds)
print('salt:', base64.b64encode(salt).decode())
print('digest:', base64.b64encode(digest).decode())

title: Detect Repeated Failed Logins in a Log
description: Count failed authentication events in a local log file.
code:
from collections import Counter

counts = Counter()
with open('auth.log', errors='replace') as f:
    for line in f:
        if 'login_failed' in line:
            fields = line.split()
            key = fields[0] if fields else 'unknown'
            counts[key] += 1
print(counts)

title: Time-Window Login Rate Limiter
description: Demonstrate a time-window limiter in memory. Use a shared store such as Redis for multi-worker production systems.
code:
from collections import defaultdict, deque
import time

history = defaultdict(deque)
WINDOW = 60
LIMIT = 5

def allow_attempt(key):
    now = time.time()
    q = history[key]
    while q and now - q[0] > WINDOW:
        q.popleft()
    if len(q) >= LIMIT:
        return False
    q.append(now)
    return True

print(allow_attempt('demo-user'))

title: TOTP Code Verification with PyOTP

title: Create a Password Audit Report CSV
description: Create a CSV report using dummy account audit results; do not store plaintext passwords.
code:
import csv

rows = [
    {'account': 'training-user-1', 'hash_scheme': 'argon2id', 'mfa_enabled': 'yes', 'finding': 'none'},
    {'account': 'training-user-2', 'hash_scheme': 'sha1', 'mfa_enabled': 'no', 'finding': 'upgrade hash and enable MFA'},
]
with open('password-audit.csv', 'w', newline='') as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=rows[0].keys())
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(rows)
print('Created password-audit.csv')
